baer-heitev/1:ד: (ד) In congregation — and R' Yehuda Azulai wrote in name of poskim to bless as individual — see there (and see in Eliyah Rabbah the text of the closing blessing on the matter).
beer-hagolah/1:ב: Tur in the name of Rambam
beer-hagolah/1:ד: Tur in the name of Tosefta
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And on the day etc. — even though its primary time is by day as written — nevertheless since he blessed at night he fulfilled, for it is no worse than if he blessed on sukkah and lulav at time of performance; and so l'chatchila one should bless at night; and once he blessed at night he does not bless by day as on sukkah as written there 46a.
beur-hagra/1:ד: (ד) And some say — that primary reading is by day as written Elohai Ekra yomam etc.; and there he wrote: all day etc.; whence do we know — as written vehayamim etc.; and for Delilah no question; and so there 1: one does not read etc. — even though gemara said when it teaches adyom — nevertheless since it taught only by day; and village children read only by day; and in Tosefta chapter 2: if he read at night he did not fulfill — R' Yosi; incident of Rabbenu Nechemiah who read in Tzipori at night — they told him there is no danger — proof.
beur-hagra/1:ה: (ה) And one etc. — Yerushalmi chapter 4: incident of R' Meir who read etc. and gave it to another and blessed on it etc. — this reads and this blesses; from here listener is like reader; as written asher karu lifnei hamelech etc.
beur-hagra/1:ט: (ט) And one does not etc. — Kol Bo in name of Yerushalmi; and it is in chapter 4 halachah 1; and in our corrupted version; and also implies there it refers only to Torah; R' Shimon ben Elazar taught the blessing etc.
beur-hagra/4:א: (א) Seif 4 — one who is etc. — because Minchah's division is night — also for Shema as Rabbenu Tam wrote Berachot 2a; and likewise for Kiddush and Havdalah as written chapter 4 there; and specifically for one who always practices like R' Yehuda there; and see Peri Chadash who divided and rejected his words.
biur-halacha/1:א: (א) Veshehecheyanu — see Mishna Berurah s.k. 1 what we wrote: some say fit to bless etc. — this is from Mor Uktzia who challenged Magen Avraham; and his words: I did not understand why this is a common matter — behold without mitzvot of mishloach manot and meal it is fit to bless shehecheyanu on the day; and even though divrei kabbalah require strengthening like Torah; and more so for an individual because of the miracle's force; and since it comes time to time it is like all festivals of the Name on which we bless shehecheyanu; and shehecheyanu does not require a cup as halacha says even in market; and Yom Kippur has no eating and drinking only sitting and rest — nevertheless we bless etc.; and he concludes there it is fine l'chatchila for one without megillah to attach shehecheyanu to cup of meal — end. But truly per his view he should bless shehecheyanu on the day itself because of the miracle — then he should also bless she'asa nissim; and I found in Meiri on Shabbat regarding Chanukah [and likewise here Purim] who wrote: one without lighting who is not where he can see — some say he blesses for himself she'asa nissim and shehecheyanu on one night and she'asa nissim all nights — words seem plausible — end. Also on his wonder at Magen Avraham — behold without mishloach manot etc. fit to bless shehecheyanu — I do not know; possible Magen Avraham agrees but he discusses when he had megillah at night and blessed shehecheyanu then and thereby fulfilled on the time itself [and what Peri Megadim supports that per Mechaber shehecheyanu at night covers mishloach manot and day meal is unclear; also forced on Magen Avraham's language]; but by day he had none — possible he agrees. Then I found in Birkat Yosef: if no megillah bless shehecheyanu but not she'asa nissim; and Rabbi the Rav [R' Yosef Molkho] — but acharonim wrote also shehecheyanu do not bless — end; I do not know which acharonim found this except Magen Avraham and Eliyah Rabbah who copied — no proof as we wrote; requires study in practice; see above siman 696 in She'arit Yosef letter 3.
biur-halacha/1:ב: (ב) Except in congregation — in Beit Yosef he wrote Orach Chayyim wrote thus in name of Yerushalmi; and see in Eliyah Rabbah who proved from several poskim one blesses even individually; and see Biur HaGra that from Yerushalmi also no proof — it refers only to Birkat HaTorah. Nevertheless it appears unfit to bless afterward since anyway this blessing even in congregation is not obligatory and depends on custom as in gemara; and who will say custom spread today to bless individually; and so Peri Megadim: safek berachot lehakel.
chatam-sofer/2:_: (there) if he became mute. NB Eliyah Rabbah rejects: above siman 140 s.k. 140 the reason is the first ones blessed before them and the last after them; here the first blessed to discharge and the closing blessing does not relate to megillah; in my view see Yerushalmi and it brings Kiddush and it is fitting here more — it teaches the reason for blessing as above: because otherwise one does not read all Torah in chapter 1 and there is no tamim unless each parashah is crowned before and after; and this unblessed afterward was not blessed before — like an open parashah; but megillah read whole — without blessing reason there is still tamim from Torah tamim; where no extra effort one may be strict like Magen Avraham.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1 — one who reads megillah blesses three blessings etc. NB I will copy here what I was asked in an incident in our community: reader became mute — does second reader start where he stopped or from beginning. Known what Magen Avraham wrote: mute — second must start from beginning. But Magen Avraham's words are wondrous: he himself finished within 24 that he need not bless anew since he intended from start to discharge entire congregation; if so examining laws Kiddushin siman 140 and Yerushalmi source of Torah reader who became mute must start from beginning — lest they say first reading was not blessed after and last not blessed before; Rosh and successors wrote this is another enactment each blesses. Implies: if not this reason — had they blessed before/after in reverse order he would start where stopped. If megillah need not bless again since he discharged congregation — why start anew. Cannot say Magen Avraham's intent is proof from Rambam who holds no blessing needed yet must start — reason as Beit Yosef siman 140 explains Yerushalmi per Rambam: starting mid-way looks like distraction. Even without blessing before, start from beginning. But most poskim argue Rambam — why Magen Avraham strict on rabbinic matter for Rambam alone. Where blessing itself depends — fine for Torah not intending to discharge many — must return and bless and start. But megillah here he discharges all and exempt from blessing — need not return; why strict rabbinically for Rambam. Even for Rambam perhaps distraction only in Torah reading where blesser does not discharge — unlike here all must fulfill with one blessing — second reader like he blessed first; for himself no concern if paused mid-reading. Yerushalmi proves only with both reasons together — first blessed before not after, last after not before; from last alone concern they not blessed before — only combined we worry. Fine in Torah with blessing after — first not blessed after. Megillah no blessing after — Harav et riveinu is not on megillah only miracle per my Sefer HaChayyim — so cannot say first not blessed after; no concern for first; from last alone insufficient — need not return. Especially Rambam: even returning he does not bless and does not fix last — only looks distracted; perhaps only because he mentioned first. Where no blessing after — no concern for first; even if read from start does not fix last — no need return for this. Rambam may agree; and for others certainly no return; safek motzi midei vaday. Need not leave majority poskim for Rambam safek. Also possible dispute on closing blessing on megillah — double safek. Will not expand. Magen Avraham brought from 484 maftir not 140 body — requires study. My ruling as written; saw Eliyah Rabbah and Degel Merubah sensed part of our words — their intent; they did not explain fully — see my library for difference — check well.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (Seif 2) one should not talk while reading it. NB see Magen Avraham what he wrote in name of Shulchan Gavoah chapter 2 Berachot — did not copy well — should finish what Shulchan Gavoah left in doubt what counts as chapters in megillah since read as iggeret — see there. In my view: since dispute in Mishnah when we read megillah — we hold from beginning — this counts between chapters — between start to Ish Yehudi and Ish Yehudi to balailah hahu etc. See my essays on Orach Chayyim from Mishnah Terumah siman 312 — wrote dispute among poskim why Rambam and Shulchan Aruch omitted this — see there and check.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [ג] [Levush] and afterward etc. Requires study from siman 484 seif 4 that l'chatchila one should not read after haftarah (Levushei Yom Tov). In my humble opinion I am there: reason of enactment to read maftir in Torah for Torah honor — if afterward reads haftarah no Torah honor; so Beit Yosef siman 482; if reader became mute mid-megillah second starts where first stopped without blessing — like shofar siman 691 seif 3; unlike Torah reader siman 140 who starts from beginning and blesses — there Levush: Birkat HaTorah enacted for itself, unlike here discharging others. One may distinguish haftarah 484 seif 5 from here. Further: there reason requires blessing before and after; closing after megillah was not enacted on megillah — unlike Magen Avraham who ruled start from beginning without blessing for all this.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [ד] Baruch Atah [the Name] Elokeinu Melech HaOlam Harav etc. — like poskim who do not say Baruch Atah [the Name] Elokeinu Melech HaOlam HaEl since already mentioned the Name and said Elokeinu; and some read HaEl; and Eliyah Rabbah ruled like Shulchan Aruch not to say; and likewise not to say in Eretz Yisrael HaEl Hanifra etc.; main other matter — see all poskim; Bach wrote to say Baruch Atah [the Name] HaEl Hanifra; even though we do not say Baruch Atah [the Name] Elokeinu Melech HaOlam HaEl — end. He was not precise: Tur and Shibbolei Leket and Agudah and Tzidah Laderech and R' David Abudraham wrote Baruch Atah [the Name] Elokeinu Melech HaOlam HaEl; even so they wrote not to say HaEl at end; and all the more per our poskim not to say at beginning; and what challenged from Knesset HaGedolah on Bach from Rambam nuschaot — undoubtedly before Bach Rambam books with Hagahot Maimoniot and Maggid printed year 3000 where wrote HaEl Hanifra. Abudraham wrote they enacted six wordings corresponding to six of Israel who fought Amalek: Harav et riveinu through Yehoshua; Vedan et dinenu through Ehud who killed Eglon king of Moav and Amon and Amalek with him; VeHoshia et amenu through Gideon Hanifra etc. through Shaul VeHishlam etc. through David; closing Hanifra etc. corresponding to Mordechai and Esther miracle; HaEl Moshi'a for future; Beit Yosef wrote another reason — see there. Minhagim: say first VeHishlam etc. then Hanifra etc. so closing is adjacent to closing; Bach challenged and Knesset HaGedolah argue all authors wrote opposite and in Minhagim — end. Abudraham gave reason why no closing like closing — see there; however in Rokeach I saw nusach like Minhagim.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (א) [Seif 1] One who reads megillah etc. — good that two men stand beside the shaliach tzibbur right and left when he reads megillah; and even fixed shaliach tzibbur takes permission before starting. Orah Vesimchah daf 25; Malach Habayit siman 31 letter 104; Ben Ish Chai parashat Tetzaveh letter 12. Meaning before blessing he says birshut mori verabotai; and custom of Chasidei Beit El YKB"TZ after chazan says birshut etc. says leshem yichud etc. behold we come to fulfill mitzvah of megillah reading to fix its root in supernal place; vihi noam etc.; then begins to bless.
levushei-serad/2:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 1 Shabbat and Yom Tov. Good to emend: and further they did not enact at all; and two reasons: one — since it is common practice one does not bless shehecheyanu; and further we see they did not enact blessing at all on mishloach manot — kal vachomer not to bless shehecheyanu on this; reason of matter: many mitzvot have no blessing as explained in many places.
levushei-serad/3:_: s.k. 2 as written siman 484 etc. in haftarah and siman 140 in Torah — reason explained siman 140: since these matters require blessing before and after — if he reads from where he stopped the first were blessed before not after and last after not before; since starting mid-way he will not say first blessing because first already blessed — therefore start from beginning and say first blessing and verses blessed before and after; per Rambam one fulfills with first's blessing — see Beit Yosef siman 140 explains Yerushalmi per his view; and siman 691 regarding shofar does not start from beginning — appears unlike Torah since shofar needs no blessing after; starts where stopped and then does not bless — as written initially. Unlike megillah which requires before and after — starts from beginning; and Magen Avraham concludes even though starts nevertheless need not bless initially since fulfills etc.; already explained Magen Avraham 484 s.k. 4; per Magen Avraham 691 distinction shofar and Torah: Torah tamim — megillah also tamim; likewise haftarah; on Magen Avraham's words there.
machatzit-hashekel/2:א: (s.k. 2) And some say etc. primary etc. by day. And above siman 687. Reason: they derive it must be read by day and night from verse in psalm Eli Eli lamah azavtani that Esther said Ekra yomam velo ta'aneh velailah velo dumiah li — trouble was day and night; therefore require publicizing miracle day and night; and since yomam written first — day is primary.
machatzit-hashekel/2:ב: (ב) If he became mute etc. siman 484. It appears the reason as Rabbenu Yonah wrote per Rambam siman 140 — and I wrote there siman 140 — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/2:ד: (ד) And likewise Mordekhai wrote in name of Rabbenu Yoel: Torah reader in congregation who talked mid-reading must return and bless — since talking is distraction; and since distracted must bless. He brought proof from Yerushalmi: Torah reader became mute — standing other must bless; therefore reason is not he did not bless yet — he fulfilled with first's blessings as Tosafot megillah R' Meir blessed on megillah then read. Rather in becoming mute reason is distraction. So too when talking mid-reading. Rabbenu Efraim disagreed distraction does not harm — when talking no need bless; but mute standing other must bless because not yet blessed — not like megillah R' Meir blessed then read — megillah different: he blessed for entire congregation — so too mute in megillah standing other need not bless.
machatzit-hashekel/3:_: (s.k. 3) Not etc. one piyyut. Meaning VeAsher He'enia is not one piyyut.
machatzit-hashekel/4:_: (s.k. 4) One should not talk. And the reader etc. — meaning plainly the listener may not talk — while talking he does not hear reader; but the reader etc. like Shema siman 66 — distinction between middle of chapter and between chapters; however he concludes in Shulchan Gavoah: requires study what counts between chapters in megillah since must read whole as iggeret — end. However in Malach Habayit parashat Kaf he read siman 20: since megillah has parashiyot even closed — nevertheless called chapters — current practice; see there.
magen-avraham/4:ב: (ב) From plag Minchah. After praying Maariv; but I would not permit tasting a little and waiting until reader comes as Berachot: one should not say I will eat a little etc. then read Shema; and stronger for megillah lest sleep seize and cancel reading — much waiting and reading is stricter obligation — all mitzvot deferred before it [Terumat HaDeshen]; and see siman 687 in name of R' Moshe of Prague: since beloved one does not neglect; and why they did not forbid learning like bedikat chametz — end. If so lenient from Shema and chametz — and since Shema and chametz permit tasting as siman 235 and 472 — kal vachomer here; and primary megillah reading is by day; and Rama changed wording wrote forbidden to eat etc. — implies tasting permitted; nevertheless do not lighten except great need; Tosefta chapter 1 Shabbat wrote megillah is like lulav and shofar and Shema; implies Maharil: even sick should not eat before reading unless danger; and simple one under duress may hear daytime reading before sunrise after alos — siman 687; Beit Yosef in name of Orach Chayyim custom read somewhat mibaal yad to ease people and pregnant not to fast excessively.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) Veshehecheyanu — proper to intend in shehecheyanu also on mishloach manot and Purim meal which are also mitzvot; inform shaliach tzibbur the blesser that listener needs intent; intend in shehecheyanu on the day since its time is daytime; one without megillah should not bless shehecheyanu on mishloach manot and meal — common matter every day Shabbat and Yom Tov [Magen Avraham]; some say fit to bless shehecheyanu on day because of miracle force; since time-bound like all moadei the Name we bless shehecheyanu; see Biur Halacha; if he had megillah at night and blessed shehecheyanu then — all agree need not bless again by day; mourner reads megillah blesses after blessings for shehecheyanu — mourner does not bless to discharge many in shehecheyanu; mourner reads megillah.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) And afterward custom to bless — gemara: closing blessing depends on custom — where custom to bless, bless; therefore Mechaber wrote nowadays custom to bless.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (ה) Harav etc. — do not say HaEl Harav since already mentioned Name saying Elokeinu; some read HaEl; Eliyah Rabbah ruled like Shulchan Aruch not to say; likewise not in Eretz Yisrael Baruch Atah [the Name] HaEl Hanifra only Baruch Atah [the Name] Hanifra — see there.
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (יג) From plag Minchah and above — it is hour and quarter before night; reason: since we consider it night for Maariv prayer one may pray then — we consider night for this too.
peri-megadim/1:א: (א) Custom — Taz: Shulchan Aruch implies so since already said "our God" siman 189; Taz proof from here see there. In some siddurim Eretz Yisrael blessing text "the great God" etc. "who completes" etc. "who redeems" etc. "in Eretz Yisrael the God who redeems His people Israel from all their troubles, the God who saves" — per Bach's nusach; Avodat Yisrael letter 4 wondered — say only "in Eretz Yisrael who redeems His people Israel from all troubles, the God who saves and redeems" near closing like a closing — see there. Explanation of blessing: Rav Abudraham and Avodat Yisrael — six fine explanations.
peri-megadim/1:ב: (ב) What he wrote in gloss one does not bless afterward individually — Eliyah Rabbah ch. 8 brought several poskim even individual blesses afterward; fit to bless without Name and Malchut — see Even HaEzer 55 Birkat Kidushin in Choshen Mishpat. And see in 5 Berachot VeAsher He'enia one says even individually without Name and Malchut.
peri-megadim/2:_: While Taz etc. his intent: what Tur brings one should not talk during reading — not to interrupt between megillah and closing blessing or mid-blessing; wants to explain Shulchan Aruch one should not talk while reading — means the blessing; and truth of Tur's language since he blesses afterward — interruption refers to blessing; but interrupting megillah certainly forbidden like Hallel and haftarah here. In gloss Terumat HaDeshen 65 understood here literally — one should not talk while reading megillah; reader who interrupts — they rebuke if not as pausing in Shema — see there.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: day. Abudraham; and see Eliyah Rabbah he need not start from beginning only from where first stopped — see there; Shulchan Aruch ch. 1 siman 42 agreed; wrote: if one says what matter starting from beginning — Chazal were very strict about tircha de tzibura etc. — only finisher should be at time of blessing first blessed as shofar siman 691 seif 3 — see there; likewise Degel Merubah megillah like shofar discharging — starts where stopped; and if only few verses read — no great tircha — start from beginning; also if majority agree start from beginning; Purim night Motzei Shabbat good to start from beginning lest souls be gloomy reading in halves; other days fast hard — lighten as Eliyah Rabbah and Shulchan Aruch start where stopped; see Shaarei Ephraim shaar 6 seif 60 and Pitchei Shearim there at start.
turei-zahav/1:_: Custom to bless Harav etc. Tur wrote in name of R' Moshe of Prague not to say HaEl since already said Elokeinu; and see siman 189 proof from here for fourth blessing in Birkat Hamazon.
turei-zahav/2:_: While reading it. This refers to the blessing; so in Tur and Bach wrote plausible etc. — after all he blesses — end; clear it refers to blessing; however Beit Yosef wrote: nevertheless this is etc. and it turns out he did not hear etc. — end; implies also on megillah; Maharshal also explained thus; challenged: why not rebuke one interrupting megillah reading — I know no source; certainly here only interrupting during blessing reading; interrupting megillah itself obviously forbidden — even in Torah forbidden b'dieved as siman 692 seif 3; kal vachomer mundane matters; nevertheless if talked even in megillah itself does not return to beginning as Rashba Beit Yosef brought — interruption only between blessing and start of megillah reading.
